items.change: Explain separate coefficient sharpness is universal only: both Lean witnesses have d=2 and nonzero information charge P/4. No sharpness claimed in growing-d, o(P) charge regime.
Qualify the first paper's asserted need for encoder and decoder savings as heuristic.

Explain that a fixed recoded-XOR broadcast is an original-row strategy with constant helper and full-cube correctness. Its interaction graph is a subgraph of G, so graph-component splitting can only decrease separator loss. State path/cycle corollary is illustrative and the bounded-degree expander obstruction is the additional reach.
items.proof: Transmit fixed packet list; every packet depends only on its one or two original rows through bijections. The fixed complete graph H is a subgraph of G. Each component of H-S lies inside a component of G-S, and sum of squares of split sizes is no larger. For a cycle, q evenly spaced separator vertices leave q blocks with sizes differing by at most one; q asymptotic to sqrt(d) gives loss (2+o(1))*b*d^(3/2). On C100 choose vertices 0,10,...,90.

items.change: State separator loss <= epsilon*P+b*K(epsilon)*d, requiring uniform component bound in d and completed run, and retain D_w+H(Z)=o(P). State expected-treewidth o(d), or a fixed ambient graph of treewidth o(d), suffices.
items.proof: If |S|<=epsilon*d and all components have size<=K, then sum_C |C|^2<=K*sum_C|C|<=K*d. Apply separator theorem, then let d grow and epsilon decrease. Fixed ambient graph contains each run graph; restrict a tree decomposition to prove monotonicity of treewidth. No stronger formal statement added.

items.change: Replace maximum possible saving with saving is at most; no matching construction or tightness claimed.
Add the sufficient independent-row-parts test, basis-extension proof, and explicit failure of necessity because same-row pairs are permitted. Do not add proposed iff.
items.counterexample: d=2,b=1, identity row recoding, broadcast all four input bits as singleton packets and x00 XOR x01 as a same-row pair. This is correct on all 16 inputs. Row0 has distinct nonzero row-parts x00,x01,x00+x01, which are dependent. All 16 cases checked. Constants also require care: model allows zero self-XOR, but no constant-one packet on a nonempty cube; fixed output shifts are decoder-equivalent normalization, not literal model identity.
items.proof_of_sufficient_condition: For each row, extend the distinct nonzero homogeneous GF(2)-linear row-parts to a basis of the dual row space; these coordinates define a linear bijection. Each homogeneous packet supported on at most two rows becomes a singleton or pair, and identically zero packets may be deleted with zeros restored by the decoder.
items.scope: For genuinely two-row homogeneous packets alone (two nonzero row-parts per packet), a restricted iff can be proved using surjectivity, but it is unnecessary here and was not inserted.

items.change: Family1 applies to finite-field variants only after explicit binary encoding, bit-cost accounting, and retaining any encoding deficit. Family2 requires actual coordinate-XOR membership after expansion; binary or extension-field linearity alone is insufficient.
items.reason: Formal inputs and packets are Boolean. An injectively encoded non-power-of-two alphabet occupies only a subfamily of the bit cube; its deficit is not zero. Infinite field symbols have no fixed finite binary representation. General GF(2^e)-linear outputs expand into GF(2)-linear forms, which need not satisfy the shared-coordinate packet restriction.
